decisions.what: TSSOP-20 has no separate VDDA or VREF+ pin: pin4=VDD/VDDA (bonded), pin5=VSS/VSSA (bonded); VREF+ is internally tied to VDD on this package.
decisions.why: Determines the decoupling network is a single VDD/VDDA-to-VSS/VSSA pair, not per-domain caps; no VREF+ cap needed.
decisions.source: DS12991 Rev4 (STM32G030x6/x8 datasheet) Section 3.7.1 Power supply schemes p.14-15, and Table 12 Pin assignment and description p.31 (pins 4,5); https://www.st.com/resource/en/datasheet/stm32g030c6.pdf

decisions.what: Decoupling: 1x 100 nF ceramic + 1x 4.7 uF across the (single) VDD/VDDA-VSS/VSSA pin pair, placed as close as possible to / below those pins.
decisions.why: This is ST's own recommended minimum decoupling network for the device, shown in the datasheet's power supply scheme figure.
decisions.source: DS12991 Rev4 Section 5.1.6 Power supply scheme, Figure 9 + Caution note, p.39; and 'General PCB design guidelines' p.70; https://www.st.com/resource/en/datasheet/stm32g030c6.pdf

decisions.what: NRST has a permanent internal pull-up (RPU, 25-55 kOhm typ 40 kOhm) - no external pull-up resistor needed.
decisions.why: External pull-up on NRST would be redundant hardware; the datasheet states the pull-up is always present.
decisions.source: DS12991 Rev4 Section 5.3.15 NRST input characteristics + Table 52, p.65; https://www.st.com/resource/en/datasheet/stm32g030c6.pdf

decisions.what: NRST minimal circuit = 0.1 uF (100 nF) filter capacitor NRST-to-GND, placed as close as possible to the device, plus a momentary push button NRST-to-GND. No other components.
decisions.why: This is ST's own 'Recommended NRST pin protection' figure/network; the push button is exactly the generic 'external reset circuit' block shown there.
decisions.source: DS12991 Rev4 Section 5.3.15, Figure 19 'Recommended NRST pin protection' and its notes 2-3, p.65-66; https://www.st.com/resource/en/datasheet/stm32g030c6.pdf

decisions.what: OPINION (not found in an ST source retrieved this session): do not oversize the NRST capacitor beyond ST's stated 100 nF - larger values (1-10 uF, sometimes added for extra debounce) are community-reported to interact badly with debug-probe 'connect under reset' / rapid reset cycling during flashing.
decisions.why: Flagged per the task's request to check for this specific footgun; AN5096 (which likely states this explicitly) could not be retrieved - see OPEN.
decisions.source: OPINION / not independently verified against an ST primary document this session; general STM32-community knowledge only

decisions.what: BOOT0 is not a dedicated pin on TSSOP-20: it is sampled on PA14 (pin 19), the same physical pin as SWCLK (and bonded with PA15).
decisions.why: Rules out any strap/jumper design that would fight the SWCLK function on this pin.
decisions.source: DS12991 Rev4 Table 12 (pin19 'PA14-BOOT0', additional functions 'ADC_IN18, BOOT0'), p.33; cross-checked against KiCad symbol MCU_ST_STM32G0.kicad_sym:STM32G030F6Px pin19 'PA14/PA15' alternate 'SYS_SWCLK (PA14)'

decisions.what: ST factory-default option byte (0xDFFFE1AA at 0x1FFF7800) decodes to nBOOT_SEL=1, nBOOT0=1, nBOOT1=1, which per the boot-mode table always selects Main Flash memory regardless of the physical BOOT0 pin state.
decisions.why: This is the single highest-value fact for this block: it means the factory-default board (with SWD-only use) needs zero BOOT0 hardware (no pull resistor, no jumper).
decisions.source: RM0454 Rev2 Section 3.4.1 FLASH option byte description, Table 9, p.59-60 (production value) and Section 2.5 Boot configuration, Table 5 Boot modes, p.47 (decode table); https://www.st.com/resource/en/reference_manual/rm0454-stm32g0x0-advanced-armbased-32bit-mcus-stmicroelectronics.pdf

decisions.what: Cross-check: the device errata sheet independently states that option-bit boot selection (nBOOT_SEL=1 and nBOOT0=1, i.e. the factory default) is required for correct Main-Flash boot under Level-1 read protection, whereas physical-pin boot selection is broken under RDP L1.
decisions.why: Second independent primary source corroborating the recommendation to leave BOOT0 handling at the factory default rather than adding pin-based strapping.
decisions.source: ES0486 Rev2 (STM32G030x6/x8 device errata) Section 2.2.3, p.4; https://www.st.com/resource/en/errata_sheet/es0486-stm32g030x6x8-device-errata-stmicroelectronics.pdf

decisions.what: RECOMMENDED: leave BOOT0/PA14 option bytes at ST factory default; wire pin19 only as SWCLK; no pull resistor, jumper, or strap on this pin.
decisions.why: Board is programmed only over SWD and never needs the BOOT0 pin to select the system bootloader; matches the factory-default behavior already verified above.
decisions.source: Derived from RM0454 Rev2 Section 2.5 Table 5 + Section 3.4.1, and ES0486 Rev2 Section 2.2.3 (see prior two decisions)

decisions.what: If the UART/system bootloader is wanted later, entry requires only an option-byte rewrite (set nBOOT0=0) performed over the existing SWD connection (e.g. STM32CubeProgrammer Option Bytes tab) - no board hardware change needed.
decisions.why: Directly answers the brief's question of what changes if the UART bootloader is desired; avoids designing in a BOOT0 strap that would conflict with SWCLK.
decisions.source: RM0454 Rev2 Section 2.5 Table 5 (row: nBOOT_SEL=1, nBOOT0=0 -> System memory), p.47; https://www.st.com/resource/en/reference_manual/rm0454-stm32g0x0-advanced-armbased-32bit-mcus-stmicroelectronics.pdf

decisions.what: Secondary corroboration (community, not load-bearing alone): STM32G0's BOOT0 pin function is disabled by default; MCU always boots main flash regardless of pin state unless option bytes are changed.
decisions.why: Independent third source agreeing with the RM0454+ES0486 conclusion above.
decisions.source: community.st.com thread 'STM32G030, Does not enter bootloader when boot0 is 3.3V...' https://community.st.com/t5/stm32-mcus-embedded-software/stm32g030-does-not-enter-bootloader-when-boot0-is-3-3v-what-is/td-p/222450 (secondary/community; used for corroboration only)

decisions.what: SWDIO = PA13 (pin18, standalone); SWCLK = PA14 (pin19, bonded with PA15/BOOT0, but PA15's alternate functions are simply unused on this board).
decisions.why: Assigns the SWD interface with no pin conflicts against UART/I2C choices below.
decisions.source: DS12991 Rev4 Table 12, p.33; cross-checked against KiCad symbol MCU_ST_STM32G0.kicad_sym:STM32G030F6Px pins 18-19

decisions.what: No external pull-up/pull-down or series resistor needed on SWDIO/SWCLK: silicon automatically activates an internal pull-up on PA13 and pull-down on PA14 whenever these pins are in the SW-debug alternate function, which is their state at every reset.
decisions.why: Removes 2-4 passives that a naive design might add; matches SWD protocol idle-state expectations (SWDIO idle-high, SWCLK idle-low) with zero components.
decisions.source: DS12991 Rev4 Table 12, footnote (5), p.34; https://www.st.com/resource/en/datasheet/stm32g030c6.pdf

decisions.what: OPINION/OPEN: no ST document defines a bare 4-pin (GND/3V3/SWDIO/SWCLK) SWD header pinout convention - ST's own debug connectors are 6-pin (add NRST+SWO). Recommend keeping requirements.md's existing GND/3V3/SWDIO/SWCLK set; most third-party probes support 4-wire SWD without a dedicated NRST wire.
decisions.why: Answers the brief's header-convention question honestly where no vendor citation exists; avoids inventing a false standard.
decisions.source: OPINION - AN5096 (which might define this) could not be retrieved this session; see OPEN items in the .md

decisions.what: UART header = USART2 on PA2 (pin9, TX) / PA3 (pin10, RX) - standalone pins, no conflict with SWD or I2C.
decisions.why: Clean pin choice with margin; matches requirements.md's existing MCU-perspective TX/RX naming.
decisions.source: DS12991 Rev4 Table 12, p.31 (pins 9-10, USART2_TX/USART2_RX alternates on PA2/PA3)

decisions.what: Choosing USART2 on PA2/PA3 for the header is not a coincidence: RM0454 states the embedded (system) bootloader listens on USART pins PA2/PA3 or PA9/PA10, so this same 4-pin UART header doubles as the bootloader UART interface with zero extra hardware if it is ever needed.
decisions.why: Reinforces the BOOT0 recommendation (software-only bootloader entry) by showing the physical UART path is already in place.
decisions.source: RM0454 Rev2 Section 2.5 Boot configuration, 'Embedded boot loader' paragraph, p.48

decisions.what: I2C bus = I2C1 with SCL on PA9 (pin16, bonded with PA11/I2C2_SCL) and SDA on PA10 (pin17, bonded with PA12/I2C2_SDA).
decisions.why: I2C1 is called out in the datasheet feature list as the more capable instance (SMBus/PMBus support, wakeup from Stop); pins are standalone-enough (bonded pair not needed simultaneously) with no conflict.
decisions.source: DS12991 Rev4 Table 12 p.32-33 (pins 16-17); feature list p.1 ('one supporting SMBus/PMBus and wakeup from Stop mode')

decisions.what: I2C1 pins (PA9/PA10) are 5V-tolerant (FT) and Fast-mode-Plus capable (_f, up to 1 Mbit/s); when configured for the I2C alternate function the GPIO output type is set open-drain in firmware (standard STM32 GPIO architecture), giving a genuine open-drain, 5V-tolerant I2C bus suitable for external pull-ups and the Qwiic downstream connector.
decisions.why: Confirms electrical suitability for a shared/multi-drop I2C bus exposed off-board.
decisions.source: DS12991 Rev4 Table 11 (I/O structure legend: FT=5V tolerant, _f=Fm+ capable) and Table 12 I/O-structure column for PA9/PA10 ('FT_f'), p.30-32

decisions.what: User LED assigned to PA5 (pin12), a standalone spare GPIO, driven through a series resistor as required by requirements.md.
decisions.why: Arbitrary but conflict-free spare-pin choice; leaves PA4/PA6/PA7/PA0/PA1 and the bonded groups on pins 1,2,3,15,20 free for margin.
decisions.source: DS12991 Rev4 Table 12 p.31 (pin12, PA5, no alternate function needed for a plain GPIO output)

decisions.what: Full 20-pin TSSOP-20 budget check: power(2) + NRST(1) + SWD(2) + UART(2) + I2C(2) + LED(1) = 9 pins/groups used, 10 spare (pins 1,2,3,7,8,11,13,14,15,20) - no conflicts.
decisions.why: Confirms the assigned peripheral set fits comfortably on this small-pin-count package with margin, the concrete deliverable requested for this block.
decisions.source: Derived from DS12991 Rev4 Table 12 (full table read pages 30-33), cross-checked pin-for-pin against KiCad MCU_ST_STM32G0.kicad_sym:STM32G030F6Px

layout_notes: Place the 100 nF + 4.7 uF decoupling pair as close as possible to VDD/VDDA(pin4)/VSS/VSSA(pin5), ideally on the board underside directly beneath the pins (DS12991 Fig.9 caution note).
Place the NRST 100 nF capacitor as close as possible to the device (DS12991 Fig.19 note 3).
No trace-length/topology constraint found for SWD/UART/I2C headers in the sources retrieved this session (AN5096 unreachable); keep short as ordinary good practice only.
PA14/pin19 (SWCLK/BOOT0/PA15) should have no pull resistor or strap added - leave it solely as the SWCLK connection to the SWD header.

errata.what: Under Flash read-protection Level 1, booting from Main Flash via the physical PA14-BOOT0 pin is not functional; option-bit boot selection (nBOOT_SEL=1, nBOOT0=1 - the factory default) works correctly.
errata.relevance: Directly supports the BOOT0 recommendation (use factory-default option-bit boot selection); no RDP Level 1 is planned for this board so the limitation itself doesn't bite, but its workaround is what we're already recommending.

errata.what: I2C wrong SDA sampling if the transmitter's data setup time is shorter than one I2C kernel-clock period; has a minimum-I2CCLK-frequency workaround.
errata.relevance: Firmware-level concern for the I2C1 bus (sensor + Qwiic); no hardware/topology change needed.

errata.what: Spurious bus-error (BERR) flag can be set in I2C master mode with no effect on the transfer; software must clear the flag.
Spurious master transfer can occur on own-slave-address match in a multi-master I2C configuration.
errata.relevance: Not applicable - this board's MCU is the only bus master on I2C1; only relevant if a Qwiic downstream device also masters the bus, which the Qwiic/STEMMA-QT convention does not do.

errata.what: USART data corruption possible from a short glitch-to-zero on the receive line within the second half of the stop bit; no workaround.
errata.relevance: Minor signal-integrity note for the UART header's RX trace; no specific hardware mitigation cited by ST beyond normal good PCB practice.
